scope: 325 language, Types, independent Analyze/Verify, ownership/borrow, Wire/Lower and CT consumers for the finite Linux x86_64 Direct scalar thread profile; independent review, not a self-review of 323 or a full async/Transfer proof
source_review: Types requires an actual static ordinary fn(i32)->i32, i32 payload and concrete zero-argument i32 closure. Callable helper/parameter entries and closure entries remain Unsupported; returning a callable result alone does not create such an entry.

Analyze and Verify independently reconstruct the actual direct worker graph. They admit only Unit/bool/u8/u16/i32/i64 storage and positive scalar opcodes, examine every CFG block, reject non-scalar storage/environment/foreign/teardown and unknown opcodes, and do not share a worker qualification proof.

Worker addresses come from real FunctionIds. Nested thread operations cannot satisfy the worker whitelist. Unrelated module declarations do not acquire a whole-module purity obligation. Normal kernel signature/SSA checks remain active.

The actual parent body is consumed under existing ownership rules; its borrowed captures remain subject to loan conflicts and scope/liveness checks. Neither the body environment nor its parent-only resources become a child payload. Reusing an owned Once body is rejected.

Wire round-trip retains the operation and actual identities. Lower consumes VerifiedModule. Both CT source/candidate paths explicitly reject the primitive; a name or producer claim does not supply migration authority.

Shared request budgets charge worker instruction/type inventories, queues and sets before growth. Analyze's ordered-set lookup/insertion is charged by bounded tree depth; Verify prepays its indexed visited vector and charges queued edges. The budget is not reset for each thread site.

The Linux adapter initializes stable scalar context before create; create failure drops the prepared parent body without invocation/join, and failed join aborts rather than returning with an active child. Successful join precedes child-result access. The focused native observer checks actual distinct pthread identity, parent-only body/drop and event order.
